environment: Launch terrain uses USGS photographic imagery and elevation around LC39A. Contemporary imagery and reconstructed launch structures do not reproduce a single historical date. Lunar terrain uses LROC Apollo 11 DTM and orthophoto; the Moon globe uses LROC imagery and LOLA elevation. Surface equipment is original simplified geometry. Historical cloud composites are not live observations. Optional Open-Meteo current weather-model values drive simplified local presets only after fresh successful retrieval; failures use a labeled preset. NOAA solar approximation supplies scenario illumination, not navigation ephemerides.

iss-interior.json.credit: NASA IGOAL ISS interior, distributed by NASA Astrobee; NASA Media Usage Guidelines.
iss-interior.json.coordinates: Source Blender metres, X corridor axis, Z up. glTF export converts to X corridor, Y up, Z=-source Y.
iss-interior.json.modifications: Restored original photographic UV textures as rough PBR materials. Original geometry/UVs/scale retained. No authored instruments or geometry added.
iss-interior.json.navigationNote: Conservative free-floating eye-position volume; source is zero-gravity module. Validate collisions at hatches and protrusions.

astronaut-reference.json.adaptation: Scaled by 0.0254 to a 1.886 m suited stature. Original UV photographic textures retained. Welded duplicate vertices for smooth normals. Head, upper torso and rear backpack excluded in first-person variants to prevent camera clipping; arms and legs statically posed by vertex transforms.
astronaut-reference.json.limitations: Reference suit model, not a photogrammetric body scan or historical Apollo A7L reproduction. No skeleton, finger articulation, reaching animation, or hand-to-control constraints.
astronaut-reference.json.coordinates: Blender Z-up, front -Y; glTF Y-up, front +Z. First-person origin at approximate pelvis (source raw centre); eye in Blender (0,-0.34,0.68), glTF (0,0.68,0.34).
astronaut-reference.json.textureRecovery: Used original uncompressed NASA revision. Its 174 out-of-range UVs caused Draco quantization to collapse the remaining suit UV detail; original retains 2131 unique UVs and correct fabric mapping.

runtimeVisualAdaptations.ModernCockpit.ts: Original procedural modern training interior: ceramic/graphite panels and three live multi-function displays. Not an operational spacecraft replica. Cabin selection does not change propulsion or make an Apollo vehicle a modern launcher.
runtimeVisualAdaptations.AstronautBody.ts: Existing NASA/DigitalSpace suit mesh with procedural hip/shoulder weights, idle, gait and reaching motion. No motion capture, finger inverse kinematics or precise hand-to-control contact.
runtimeVisualAdaptations.CoastalLandscape.ts: USGS measured heightfield interpolated bilinearly, with original grass clumps placed from a green imagery mask. Vegetation and buildings are reconstructed, not surveyed current objects.
runtimeVisualAdaptations.lighting: Authored solar, night/twilight and ocean-highlight shaders using approximate scenario solar direction; real-time GPU rendering. No generated raster images added.
runtimeVisualAdaptations.VehicleDetail.ts: AI-assisted original surface detailing for the fictional orbital trainer: coating microtexture, reflective window material, cable raceways, interstage vents, capture latches, RCS nozzle inserts, thermal-shield edge and service radiator slats. These visual additions do not establish real vehicle specifications or add simulated capabilities. No NASA or commercial launch-provider branding. Saturn V and Apollo reference assets are unchanged.
